summary: This unit teaches you to prepare and serve non-alcoholic beverages in a villa: plan and set up a beverage station, work safely and hygienically, make coffee (filter, French press, espresso, milk drinks), brew black, green and herbal teas, make Jamaican chocolate tea, prepare fresh juices, smoothies, sorrel and mocktails, serve drinks correctly, look after guests with special dietary needs, handle complaints, clean the equipment and close down.

blocks.p: A good cup of coffee or a cold glass of sorrel is often the first thing a guest enjoys at a villa. Beverages look simple, but they are easy to spoil: coffee that is bitter, tea that is stewed, juice that is warm, a glass with a chip. This unit is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees. You learn to make drinks that taste right, are safe, and are served with care.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and group practical tasks in the Centre: a villa breakfast with coffee, tea, bush tea and chocolate tea, and a pool-side cold-drinks bar with a juice, a smoothie, a mocktail and iced tea or sorrel. The assessor watches your hygiene, safety, method, serving and clean-up.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.note: Maker's instructions differ between machines and products. Where this kit gives a time, a temperature or an amount, it is a typical figure. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and your instructor.
blocks.label: Tip

blocks.p: **Mise en place** (French for 'put in place') means having all the tools and ingredients ready and in position **before service**. A prepared station lets you serve quickly and calmly.

flow: Check the booking: numbers and special requests
Switch on and check the equipment
Stock cups, glasses, spoons, napkins, trays
Fill sugar, sweetener, milk jugs, lemon slices
Prepare and chill juice; fill the ice bin with a scoop
Check the area is tidy and safe

head: Equipment
Used for
Check before use
rows: Clean, water level, steam wand, group head, drip tray
Holding and pressing the ground coffee
Grinding beans to the right grind
Lid, jug and blades clean; secure
Clean scoop; clean bin; never a glass

ul: Use **first in, first out**: put new cartons of milk or juice **behind** the older ones so that the older stock is used first.
Keep milk and fresh juice at **5 °C or below**, or as the Centre's food safety plan says.
Keep coffee beans and tea in sealed, dry containers away from heat, light and strong smells.
Label, cover and date anything you prepare.
Check use-by dates every day.

blocks.p: Brew coffee **a few minutes before serving** so it is fresh and hot. Coffee made the night before, or left on a hot plate for an hour, tastes stale and bitter. Brew tea to order. Squeeze juice shortly before service, or store it correctly.

sections.title: Hygiene and safety at the beverage station

ul: Clean uniform, hair tied back, short clean nails, no jewellery that could fall in the drink.
**Wash your hands** before work, after touching your face or hair, after the toilet, after clearing and after handling waste or money.
Report illness. Do not handle food or drink if you have vomiting or diarrhoea.
Hold cups and glasses by the body or the base, never by the rim or inside.
A **Food Handler's Permit** from the local health department is required for every food and drink handler in Jamaica.

head: Rule
Why
rows: Use an ice scoop, never a glass or your hands
Glass can chip or break and leave pieces in the ice; hands spread germs
If a glass breaks near the ice bin: empty the bin, melt the ice away, clean it and refill
Tiny pieces are hidden in the ice
Keep milk and fresh juice at 5 °C or below
Cover, label and date prepared juice
So it is not kept too long and allergens are known
Cut on a stable board with a sharp knife, cutting away from your hand
Blunt knives and unstable boards cause cuts
Use a separate clean cloth for the counter and for the cups

head: Hazard
Control
rows: Never overfill; keep hands clear of the spout; carry hot water with care
Keep hands clear of the tip; purge before and after use; wipe with a clean damp cloth
Dry hands; check plugs and cables; report faults and do not use faulty equipment
Fit the lid, start slowly, and **switch off and unplug** before lifting the jug or touching the blades; never push food down with a spoon while it runs; do not fill to the top
Wipe spills at once; put out a wet-floor sign
Read the label and the **safety data sheet (SDS)**; wear gloves; never mix chemicals

blocks.note: If you scald your hand with hot water, cool it under cool running water for about 20 minutes. Do not put butter or oil on it, do not burst blisters and do not rub ice straight on the burn. Tell your supervisor and fill in the accident book.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: Milk, soy, nuts (including some syrups and plant milks), gluten (some malt drinks) and fruit can cause allergic reactions. Ask guests about allergies and read labels. Clean the blender and jugs between orders.

blocks.h: The coffee plant and Jamaican coffee

blocks.p: Jamaica's best-known coffee is grown in the **Blue Mountains**. Coffee is sold as beans, which are ground just before brewing. Fresh grinding keeps the flavour.

head: Method
Grind
Looks like
Why
rows: Water passes quickly under pressure and needs fine particles
Coffee stays in the water for minutes; a fine grind would be bitter and pass through the plunger

flow: Add the right amount of coffee (follow the maker's guide)
Pour water just off the boil (about 90–96 °C)
Press the plunger slowly or remove the filter
Serve at once in warm cups
Wipe the portafilter dry and fill with freshly ground fine coffee
Flush the group head briefly and lock in the portafilter
Stop at the right volume and serve

ul: A good single shot takes about **25 to 30 seconds** (follow the maker's guide). It has a golden-brown layer of foam on top called **crema**.
Water in an espresso machine is hot and under pressure; do not take the portafilter out while the shot is running.

head: Problem
Likely cause
Cure
rows: Pours very slowly, bitter and burnt taste
Ground too fine or pressed in too hard
Use a coarser grind or lighter tamp
Pours very fast (under about 15 seconds), thin, sour and weak
Ground too coarse, too little coffee, or tamped too lightly
Use a finer grind, correct dose and firm tamp
Old coffee or the wrong grind
Use fresh beans and adjust the grind
Machine not hot enough, or cold cup
Allow the machine to warm; warm the cups

ul: Use **cold** milk in a clean, cold jug.

Purge the steam wand briefly, put the tip just below the surface, and open the steam. Introduce a little air for foam, then lower the tip to heat. Stop at about 60–65 °C (when the jug is too hot to hold comfortably).
**Do not boil milk.** Overheated milk tastes burnt and the foam soon goes flat.
Straight after steaming, **wipe the wand with a clean damp cloth and purge** a short burst of steam so milk does not dry inside.

head: Drink
What it is
rows: Espresso with steamed milk and a thick layer of milk foam
Espresso with a lot of steamed milk and a thin layer of foam
Hot water poured over ground coffee in a paper filter
Coffee with most of its caffeine removed

blocks.note: Offer plant milk (soy, oat) to guests who cannot drink cow's milk, after checking the label. Evaporated milk and condensed milk are cow's milk products.
blocks.label: Remember

sections.title: Tea, bush teas and chocolate tea

flow: Fill the kettle with fresh, cold water and boil
Warm the teapot with a little hot water and pour it out
Add tea (usually one teaspoon of leaves or one bag per cup, as the maker says)

ul: Use **freshly drawn** water, just boiled. Do not use water that boiled earlier or water from the hot tap.
**Warm the teapot** so the water stays hot and the tea brews properly.
Do not leave tea in the pot for more than a few minutes or it becomes bitter.

head: Tea
Water
Time
Notes
rows: Serve with milk, sugar or lemon
Water that is too hot makes it bitter
Herbal or 'bush' tea (fever grass or lemongrass, ginger, mint)
Boiling water poured over, or simmered

blocks.p: **Chocolate tea** is a hot breakfast drink made from grated balls of pure local cocoa. It is simmered gently in water (and sometimes milk) with spices such as cinnamon and nutmeg, and sweetened. It is not made from instant coffee powder, pimento berries or sorrel. Methods differ from cook to cook, so follow the villa's recipe.
A tray for a guest holds the pot of tea, a cup and saucer, a teaspoon, milk, sugar and lemon slices, and a napkin. Coffee plungers, cocktail stirrers and blender jugs do not belong on it.
Brew the tea double strength, strain, cool, then pour over ice with lemon. Keep it covered and chilled.

sections.title: Cold drinks: juices, smoothies, sorrel and mocktails

ul: Wash the fruit, cut or squeeze, strain if the guest wants it, and serve cold.
Common Jamaican juices: orange, June plum, soursop, carrot, cane.
Store spare juice **covered, labelled and dated** in the fridge at 5 °C or below. Do not leave it in an open jug on the counter, near the coffee machine or in the ice bin.

flow: Add fruit, a little liquid (juice, milk or yoghurt) and ice to the blender jug
Start slowly, then blend until smooth
Switch off, unplug if you are lifting the jug, and pour

blocks.p: The Jamaican **sorrel** drink is made by steeping the dried red sepals (often called petals) of the sorrel (hibiscus) plant in hot water with ginger and sometimes pimento, then sweetening and chilling. It is often served at Christmas. It is not made from roots, green leaves or seeds.
A **mocktail** is a mixed fruit drink made **without alcohol**. A 'virgin' piña colada is made without rum, using pineapple (its main flavour) and coconut.

head: Mocktail
Ingredients (typical)
rows: Mixed juices, a little syrup, ice, slices of fruit
Pineapple juice, coconut cream, ice, blended
Fresh ginger, lime juice, sugar, soda water, ice

ul: **Carbon dioxide** makes soft drinks and soda water fizzy.
Open a sealed bottle of water at the table and pour in front of the guest.

head: Glass
Use
rows: Tall juices, soft drinks and mocktails with ice

ul: Put the **ice in the glass first**, then pour the drink.
Measure ingredients so every drink tastes the same.
Add a neat garnish (a slice of lime, a mint leaf). Use a coaster under the glass.
Clean and polish the rim; never serve a chipped glass.

sections.title: Serving drinks, special needs and complaints

ul: Greet, ask what the guest would like, and **repeat the order back**: 'Coffee, black, no sugar.'
Do not add milk because most people take it, or ask a colleague what the guest drank yesterday.
Ask about allergies or dietary needs.
Serve drinks from the guest's **right**, using your right hand where possible.
Hold glasses by the base or stem; hold cups by the handle or saucer.
Hot drinks go in **cups that are clean and warmed beforehand**, not wet from the dishwasher, cold from the fridge or chipped.
Turn the cup handle to the guest's right.
Carry a loaded tray on the **palm**, with the heaviest items near your body. Do not carry high above the head or tucked under your arm.
Keep drinks away from paperwork and electronics.

head: Need
What to offer
rows: Plant milk such as soy or oat (check the label)
Unsweetened drinks, sweetener, water; do not add sugar; do not guess
Check every syrup, plant milk and garnish; clean the blender; tell the cook and the team
Smaller portions, warm (not hot) milk, a lid or non-breakable cup

flow: Take the drink and replace it

head: Complaint
Best response
rows: Apologise, remove it and bring a fresh hot pot. Do not add hot water at the table, blame the guest or offer a cold drink instead
Apologise, remake it with fresh coffee, and find the cause (grind, time, old coffee)
Apologise, remove it, check the date and the fridge, and tell the supervisor

ul: Wipe the counter and the steam wand after each use.
Rinse jugs immediately after use, because milk dries hard.
Empty the drip tray and the knock box when needed.

head: Item
How
rows: **Backflush** the group head with a blind basket and detergent as the maker says; rinse; clean the portafilters and baskets; wipe the steam wand; empty the drip tray
**Unplug it**, wash, rinse and dry the jug and blades; do not rinse the blades with your fingers under the hot tap; do not wipe the motor base under running water
**Descale** as the maker says: this removes the hard white mineral build-up from the water
Empty, clean, sanitise and refill as house rules say
Wash, rinse, dry and store clean and covered
Wipe, sweep, mop; put out a wet floor sign

blocks.note: Descaling and cleaning chemicals can burn the skin and eyes. Read the label and the safety data sheet (SDS), wear gloves and eye protection if the label says, never mix chemicals and rinse the machine well afterwards.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: Cover, label and date stock. Put milk and juice in the fridge at 5 °C or below. Keep dry goods sealed.
Report to your supervisor: **equipment faults and items running low**. Do not report which guests did not tip or which drank most coffee.
Record temperatures, cleaning and faults in the logbook.

Switch off and unplug what should be off

c1.title: A rushed morning in Mandeville
c1.text: At a villa in Mandeville, trainee Kayla arrives at 6:30 a.m. to prepare breakfast drinks for ten guests who will sit down at 8:00. A delivery of milk arrived yesterday and is in the fridge in front of the older cartons. The filter coffee machine has a little old coffee in the jug. The urn is almost full. The head of the villa asks for fresh coffee at 8:00.

c2.title: An espresso machine that is not right
c2.text: Trainee Devon is making cappuccinos on the villa's espresso machine. His shots pour in about 8 seconds and look pale and thin, with little crema, and taste sour. He has used the same grinder setting since yesterday. Mrs. Palmer, the guest, is waiting. Devon also has to steam the milk.

c3.title: A tea order on a verandah in Port Antonio
c3.text: Two guests on a verandah in Port Antonio order tea: Mrs. Reid wants a pot of black tea with milk, and Mr. Reid wants green tea. Later Mr. Reid asks whether the villa serves 'bush tea' and what it is.

c4.title: A pool-side drinks bar at a villa in Negril
c4.text: At a pool-side event, trainee Alicia makes a smoothie, a fresh orange juice and a virgin piña colada. She has made too much orange juice and leaves a jug of it on the counter near the coffee machine for the next three hours. Later, a glass breaks near the ice bin when a guest knocks it, and the blender has a tough piece of frozen fruit stuck on the blades.

c5.title: Guests with different needs
c5.text: At a villa in St Ann, Mr. Facey is diabetic, Mrs. Facey is allergic to tree nuts, and their son Tyrone, aged 6, wants a hot drink. Mrs. Facey asks for a latte made with almond milk. The cook says the sorrel has been sweetened.

c6.title: Closing down the beverage station
c6.text: At the end of the shift Raheem closes down the beverage station at a villa in Treasure Beach. The espresso machine has milk on its steam wand, the blender is still plugged in with water in the jug, and the kettle shows a hard white crust inside. A bottle of descaler is on the shelf.

questions.q: Kayla is told ten guests are coming. What should she check before she sets up?
o: Whether the cups match the colour of the plates
The guest list and any special requests, such as decaf
How many guests wrote a review the month before
Whether the guests have left a tip on earlier stays
questions.why: Knowing numbers and special requests lets her stock enough cups, milk and alternatives. The other options do not affect the drinks.

questions.q: What should Kayla do first at the filter coffee machine?
o: Reheat the old coffee and top it up with some new coffee
Brew now and keep the jug on the hot plate until 8:00
Rinse the old coffee out with a little hot water and brew
Pour away the old coffee, wash the jug, brew just before 8:00
questions.why: Old coffee tastes stale. Coffee is brewed a few minutes before serving, in a clean jug, so it is fresh and hot.

questions.q: Kayla finds a carton of juice in the fridge that is a day past its use-by date. What should she do?
o: Throw it away and tell her supervisor
Boil it and use it in the smoothies
Use it for the staff before the guests arrive
Serve it only to guests who ask for juice
questions.why: Out-of-date juice is not safe to serve to anyone. It is thrown away and the supervisor told so stock checks can be improved.

questions.q: Why should Kayla check that the urn is not overfilled?
o: The water will taste bitter
The urn will use more electricity
Boiling water can splash and scald
The tea will brew too fast
questions.why: An overfilled kettle or urn can spill hot water and cause scalds, so it is never overfilled.

questions.q: What is the most likely cause of Devon's pale, sour, fast shots?
o: The coffee is ground too fine and tamped too hard
The milk is too hot
The coffee is ground too coarse or tamped too lightly
The cup is too warm
questions.why: Water passing quickly through coarse or loose coffee gives a thin, sour shot. A shot that is too slow and bitter has the opposite problem.

questions.q: What should Devon change first?
o: Grind finer and tamp firmly and evenly
Grind coarser and tamp lightly
Use less coffee in the basket
Use a cooler cup
questions.why: A finer grind and a firm tamp slow the water so it extracts more flavour. About 25 to 30 seconds is the target.

questions.q: Devon steams the milk for Mrs. Palmer's cappuccino. What should he do?
o: Boil the milk first and then whisk the foam by hand
Hold the wand deep in the jug until the milk boils
Use milk kept warm on the hot plate to save time
Use cold milk in a cold jug and stop at about 60–65 °C
questions.why: Overheated milk tastes burnt and the foam goes flat. Cold milk and a clean jug give the best foam.

questions.q: After steaming, what should Devon do with the wand?
o: Leave it in the jug so that the milk stays warm
Wipe it with a damp clean cloth and purge a little steam
Wrap it in a dry towel until the next order
Wipe it only at the end of the shift, once cool
questions.why: Milk dries and blocks the wand if left. Wipe and purge straight away.

questions.q: How should the pot of black tea be made for Mrs. Reid?
o: Add tea to a cold pot and use warm tap water for 15 minutes
Warm the pot, add tea, pour on boiling water, brew 3 to 5 minutes
Brew it for only 10 seconds so that it stays light
Use water that boiled an hour ago to save a little time
questions.why: Fresh, just-boiled water, a warmed pot and about 3–5 minutes give a good cup. Old or warm water and very short or long times spoil it.

questions.q: Later the guests ask for iced tea. What is the best way to make it?
o: Brew it normally and pour it hot over a full glass of ice
Make it with cold water and leave it standing overnight
Brew it double strength, strain, cool, then pour over ice with lemon
Use warm tap water and a few tea leaves
questions.why: Double strength tea allows for the ice that will melt into it, so the drink is not weak. Cooling before serving keeps it clear and fresh.

questions.q: What is 'bush tea'?
o: A herbal tea made from local plants such as fever grass
A black tea blend that is imported from India
A tea made by stirring instant coffee into hot milk
A fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger and sorrel
questions.why: Bush tea is a Jamaican herbal tea made from plants such as fever grass (lemongrass). It is caffeine-free.

questions.q: What should Alicia have done with the spare orange juice?
o: Left it covered on the counter so that it stays fresh
Poured it into the ice bin so that it stays very cold
Kept it beside the coffee machine to stay nicely warm
Covered, labelled and dated, in the fridge at 5 °C or below
questions.why: Juice spoils if kept warm. It must be cooled, covered, labelled and dated.

questions.q: Alicia wants to garnish the virgin piña colada. Which garnish is best?
o: A cherry that has been soaked in rum
A lime slice cut earlier and left on the counter
A pineapple wedge taken with bare fingers from an open bowl
A wedge of washed pineapple cut on a clean board
questions.why: A fresh garnish, cut hygienically, adds flavour and looks good. Anything with alcohol or left in the open is not suitable for a non-alcoholic drink.

questions.q: How should Alicia free the frozen fruit stuck on the blender blades?
o: Push it free with a spoon while the blender still runs
Switch off and unplug it first, then remove the jug
Pull it free with her fingers while the jug is on the base
Add more ice and run the blender faster until it clears
questions.why: A blender is switched off and unplugged before anyone touches the jug or blades. Blades can cause serious cuts.

questions.q: What should the server offer Mr. Facey, who is diabetic, for his tea or coffee?
o: Tea or coffee already sweetened with two spoons of sugar
The sorrel, since it is a juice and so a healthy drink
Unsweetened drinks or sweetener, leaving sugar to him
A sweet fruit juice with plenty of ice to dilute it
questions.why: Diabetic guests need to avoid sugar, so offer unsweetened options. Do not guess or add sugar.

questions.q: Mrs. Facey asks for a latte with almond milk. What should the server do?
o: Not use it, since almonds are nuts, and offer another milk
Make it, as almond milk is only a drink and not a nut
Make it but use only a small amount in the cup
Make it and tell her it is safe without checking
questions.why: Almonds are tree nuts, so almond milk would be dangerous for a tree nut allergy. Offer a safe alternative, such as soy or oat milk if the label is clear.

questions.q: How should the hot drink for Tyrone, aged 6, be served?
o: Warm, not hot, in a safe cup with a lid if possible
As hot as the adults' drinks, so that it stays hot
In a glass, so that he can see what is in the drink
Placed at the very edge of the table within his reach
questions.why: A child could be scalded, so drinks are warm rather than hot and served in a safe cup.

questions.q: How should Raheem finish with the blender?
o: Leave it plugged in with water in the jug overnight
Rinse the blades with his fingers under the hot tap
Wipe the motor base under running water
Unplug it, then wash, rinse and dry the jug and blades
questions.why: A blender is unplugged before cleaning. The motor base must never be put under water.

questions.q: What should Raheem use to remove the white crust inside the kettle?
o: Strong washing-up liquid and a metal scouring pad
A descaling product, used as the maker says, with gloves
Bleach, poured in and left to stand overnight
Two cleaning products mixed together for more power
questions.why: The white crust is mineral scale, which is removed by descaling. Never mix chemicals, and follow the maker's instructions and the safety data sheet.

questions.q: Raheem notices the fridge thermometer reads 9 °C. What should he do?
o: Carry on, because the milk still feels cold to touch
Move the thermometer to the door shelf of the fridge
Tell the supervisor at once and check the milk and juice
Turn the fridge off for the night to save electricity
questions.why: Milk and juice must be at 5 °C or below. A fridge that is too warm can allow bacteria to grow, so the supervisor must know and the stock must be checked.
